title: cerastium semidecandrum subsp. dentatum
intro: Cerastium semidecandrum subsp. dentatum, commonly known as the toothed mouse-ear chickweed, is a plant species within the carnation family (Caryophyllaceae) that is native to Europe and Western Asia. The toothed mouse-ear chickweed plant is valued for its potential health benefits, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which can aid in soothing skin irritations, reducing fever, and fighting off infections. The therapeutic actions of this plant include its ability to act as an expectorant, helping to relieve respiratory issues such as coughs and congestion, and its anti-inflammatory properties, which can reduce swelling and pain. The bioactive constituents present in Cerastium semidecandrum subsp. dentatum include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
